ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $a\parallel b$, $\angle 1=\angle 2$, $\angle 3=40^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle 4$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $a \parallel b$,\\
it follows that $\angle 1 + \angle 2 + \angle 3 = 180^\circ$,\\
since $\angle 3 = 40^\circ$,\\
then $\angle 1 + \angle 2 = 180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ$,\\
given that $\angle 1 = \angle 2$,\\
thus $\angle 2 = 70^\circ$,\\
since $a \parallel b$,\\
it concludes that $\angle 4 = \angle 2 = \boxed{70^\circ}$.
